whatis.intro: A wholesale markup is what a distributor adds to its landed cost to set the price it charges its accounts. It is stated as a share of cost. A 35% markup on a $22.00 case gives a $29.70 wholesale price, before the account adds its own.

cards.title: Where it sits in the chain
cards.body: Between your supplier and your account. The store or kitchen adds its own markup on top of your price, so yours is one step of several.
cards.alt: Warehouse, for where a wholesale markup sits in the chain

cards.title: Street accounts
cards.body: Independent accounts usually buy off your price list at the markup you choose. They tend to carry more margin, and more cost to serve per case.
cards.alt: Map pin, for street accounts priced off your list

cards.title: Contract accounts
cards.body: Chains and groups often buy at landed cost plus a set markup or a fee per case. A fixed fee does not grow when cost rises, so its margin thins.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for contract accounts on cost plus a fee

look.h2: Check the mix before you budget on the blend
look.intro: The blend is only as true as the split you type. Anyone building a budget on it should settle these three questions first.

steps.title: Staple share in dollars, not cases
steps.body: Weight the 60% by sales dollars. Staples are often the cheaper cases, so a share counted in cases overstates their pull on the blend.

steps.title: One markup that stands for specialty
steps.body: The 35% stands in for every line that is not a staple. If those lines carry different markups, type one combined markup: their total profit divided by their total cost.

steps.title: Contract sales at their own rate
steps.body: Cases sold to chains on cost plus a fee do not carry your list markup. Leave them in at 35% and the blend reads wrong, usually high.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits in your sales mix
vos.h3: Reps free to sell, not take orders
vos.body: VOS does not calculate markups or measure your blend. Routine order taking moves off your reps: orders arrive confirmed once customers place them by voice in the VOS app.
